title: THE EMBASSY THAT HATCHED
author: GPT

rounds.summary: Gives the day its large, strange and physical register after a human civic opening: a building that is also an egg, nine hundred guests, three city blocks and a five-hour clock. Ambassador Teth has a coherent, honourable belief (the child needs the assembled community's breath and memory, and evacuation would declare it unwanted), so the conflict is between two goods rather than good and bad. The insight that the egg needs the community's patterned presence, not their physical confinement, is a genuine reframe of what the problem is; the solution is developmental engineering and hospitality, a different kind of intelligence from S1's materials evidence. Every guest, Teth, the city and the emerging being can refuse. The positive result is clear: all guests out, blocks spared, a child born responsive to both peoples.

A strong, living draft. The mechanism is the best thing in it: the child answers live, reciprocal attention and not a recording (Jo plays the recording and nothing happens), so Teth's belief that confinement makes a witness is tested and found wrong on the page, and Eren answering his mother through the wall is a real, small, felt moment. Suil's line 'The rite never had a cordon' is the turn of the story and it comes from a counterpart with standing, not from Illuminara. Costs are named and the ending is a real positive result. Three things remain. (1) Teth's last stated fear, that outside the shell Vaeli law may not recognise the hatching, is never answered, so her step into the valve reads as pressure from a closing passage and Mara's anger rather than as understanding. (2) Illuminara's own decisive contribution is thin and partly narrated: Jo, Mara, Suil and Kher supply most of the solving moves, and her key insight is told in a summary paragraph after Jo and Mara have already shown it. (3) The last scene lands its best beats (Teth's two truths, Vey's 'I believe you', Eren and the newborn) but surrounds them with an administrative run and three restatements of the moral; the whole story is about 4,400 words by my rough count, nearly twice the usual range.

A clear step up. All three T02 points were genuinely applied: Illuminara now designs the live-versus-recorded test before the confirming evidence (a recording with no listener fails, a sentence only Eren's mother can finish succeeds); Suil and Kher answer Teth's strongest fear from inside Vaeli law, and Teth crosses with the passage still open; the story is about a quarter shorter and ends on Eren and the newborn. The mechanism, the counterpart agency and the costs are all intact. Three smaller things remain, none of them structural.

final_critic_line: Illuminara discovers that the unborn child needs freely answered presence rather than captive bodies, then protects a moving welcome without choosing for Teth or the newborn; all nine hundred guests leave, the city survives, Vaeli witnesses carry the rite outside and the child gains a lawful habitat with a route back.
